On the standing dev box, `cd papercusp-desktop && npm run dev` runs
`bin/desktop-dev-nohmr`, which launches `tauri dev` with `devUrl` overridden to
**:3070** (you'll see the running proc as `npm run tauri dev --config {"build":{"devUrl":"http://localhost:3070"}}`).
The :3070 Hono host serves the **BUILT** `apps/operator-vite/dist/`, kept fresh by
a `vite build --watch`. So the desktop webview is **NOT** the :3055 HMR dev server.

Consequences for verifying an operator-vite (SPA) change in the desktop:
- A source edit reaches the webview only after the `vite build --watch` rebuilds
  `dist/` (a few seconds) **and** the webview is reloaded (Ctrl+R) — there is **no
  live HMR** in the desktop. (`:3055` HMR still exists and compiles, but the
  desktop doesn't load it.) If a fresh webview load shows
  *"operator-vite is not built…"* you caught it mid-rebuild — reload after the
  watch finishes.
- A `papercusp-desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` change (e.g. `dragDropEnabled`)
  is a Rust/window-config change: it needs a **binary recompile + window restart**,
  which the running `tauri dev` does automatically when it sees the file change
  (fast incremental relink). A webview reload alone does NOT apply it.

Isolated-instance gotcha (for [[feedback_own_xvfb_for_e2e]] /
[[feedback_drive_desktop_with_tauri_agent_tools]]): a 2nd `tauri dev` under Xvfb
safely **reuses** the running backend (beforeDevCommand `dev-operator-ifneeded.sh`
skips the spawn when :3055 is bound; dev mode skips the sidecar). Its
tauri-agent-tools bridge port is auto-assigned (read the real port/token from
`/tmp/tauri-dev-bridge-<pid>.token`; `--port/--token` go on the **subcommand**,
e.g. `eval --port …`). BUT bridge-eval `fetch`es to authed operator endpoints
return **403** in the 2nd instance (no authed session/workspace) — so
data-dependent UI (e.g. `plans:list` → the PlanRail rows) won't load there. Good
for routing/render checks (the route resolves, the component mounts); not for
data-driven UI. Verify data-driven UI with a unit test or in the user's authed
window instead.

Before trusting ANY live measurement (curl results, eval-harness numbers, "is my fix working"), verify the server process is actually the fresh one running your current code + env. Check the PID and start time (`ss -tlnp | grep :PORT`, then `ps -o lstart= -p PID`).

**Why (2026-05-29, Restart search):** I burned an entire long turn chasing a phantom "regression" — "canon camera → toner #1", 37ms responses, a harness run of P@5 0.718 with 2 guardrail failures — and wrote those bad numbers into plan commits. Root cause was operational, not code: the `:3100` shop-api was an **orphaned process** (started hours earlier) that `bin/overmind-all restart shop-api` did NOT control (there were several stale duplicate overmind instances on different sockets/tmux). Every "restart" I ran was a silent no-op; the zombie kept serving old code AND a stale `LLM_RERANK=0` env left over from a diagnostic. The code had been correct the whole time — killing the zombie + launching fresh fixed it instantly.

**How to apply:**
1. A suspiciously **fast** response is the tell: if a path should call a reranker/LLM (~1-2s) but returns in tens of ms, the rerank code isn't running — suspect a stale process or wrong route BEFORE suspecting the code.
2. After any restart, confirm the PID changed and start-time is recent. Don't assume `overmind restart`/`overmind-all restart` worked — orphans + multiple overmind instances make it no-op.
3. If a "regression" appears right after you toggled an env var for a diagnostic (e.g. flipped `LLM_RERANK=0` for a probe), suspect the toggle didn't get restored into the *actually-serving* process.
4. To force a known-good state: `kill <pid-on-port>`, then launch directly (`PORT=… node --env-file=.env node_modules/.bin/tsx apps/<svc>/src/main.ts`) and test that instance.
5. Don't commit measured numbers until the serving process is verified fresh. [[feedback_per_turn_commit]] is about committing code, not unverified metrics.

**Papercup operator instance (2026-05-30):** the running operator API on `:3070` is `tsx bin/hono-host.ts` (a long-running tsx process with NO file-watch); `dev:operator` → operator-vite `vite build --watch` is only the FRONTEND. So edits to `apps/operator/lib/**` (e.g. agent-tools) do NOT go live until that hono-host process is restarted — module singletons (like `coordLog`) were eval'd at startup. Verifying "is my server code live": send through the live tool and check WHERE the write landed (during the coord FS→PG port, a `coord:send` landing in `coord/*.jsonl` instead of `harness_shared.coord_event_log` proved the operator was still on the pre-cutover code). Restarting hono-host also resets the papercusp-su MCP session, so it's the user's call, not mine to do unilaterally.

Restart **Scout** (`apps/scout-service`, :3350) DEFAULT is now **gpt-4o-mini** (`callOpenAI`, OpenAI
endpoint, `OPENAI_API_KEY` in .env) — switched from gemini-2.5-flash for reliable native function-
calling + far fewer 503s, at ~half the (tiny) cost. SupportedModel = `qwen3.5` | `gemini-flash-2.0`
| `groq` | `gpt-4o-mini` (all selectable via the `model` param; `DEFAULT_MODEL` in scout.types.ts).
(xAI **Grok** was added then removed — git-recoverable from commit 8b82a191.)

**The fix that made gemini reliable — FORCED function-calling (Option A), in `callGemini`:** on the
FIRST detection round only, append a `respond_to_user` sentinel tool + set `tool_choice:'required'`.
gemini-2.5-flash treats native tool-calls as optional under `tool_choice:'auto'` — it would reply in
prose and SKIP the obvious tool (search/prefill/open_drawer), then sometimes hallucinate it had acted.
Forcing a choice between the real tools and the sentinel removes that escape hatch. The sentinel call
means "no action, just reply" → filtered out → the streaming prose round runs. **Force round-0 only:**
forcing every round makes the model re-call the action in a loop (open_drawer fired 5× → MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS);
later rounds use `auto` so the turn terminates. Result: search **4/4**, prefill **2/2** (3rd was a 503),
open_drawer **1×**, chitchat streams a normal reply — and the real-browser /quote prefill that used to
fail now fills the form. A deterministic detection temp (0.1) is also set.

Forced function-calling is shared by both OpenAI-compat providers (gpt-4o-mini + gemini) via the
`RESPOND_SENTINEL` const + `forceTool` on round 1. gpt-4o-mini's native function-calling is strong, so
forcing is belt-and-suspenders there; for gemini it was essential.

**Gotcha — telemetry vs the least-privilege DB role:** scout connects as **`restart_app`** (DATABASE_URL),
which has INSERT/SELECT but **NO CREATE on schema public**. `TelemetryService.ensureSchema()` ran
`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` on every boot → denied → it flipped `degraded=true` and recorded NOTHING
(cost/usage) for ALL models. Fixed: on DDL failure, probe `to_regclass` — if the tables exist (always, on
deployed DBs), keep telemetry ON (INSERTs work). Lesson: any runtime DDL under `restart_app` fails; do
schema in migrations (privileged), not at boot.

Residual flakiness on gemini is ONLY Google 503s (infra, not routing); gpt-4o-mini avoids those.

**Testing:** Scout e2e = **verdict** (Tauri docs are papercup-only — Restart has no Tauri app). Drive the
browser chat (gemini default now routes reliably), or hit `/chat/stream` with `model:"gemini-flash-2.0"`,
or bypass the LLM via `POST /tooldef/mcp` with `x-service-key`/`x-on-behalf-of-customer`. `qwen3.5` also
reliable if needed. Governed surface (all `@papercusp/tooldef`): catalog.search, orders.serials/assets.list
(off serial_scan, customer-scoped); client tools open_drawer (cart `shop:cart-open`, quote new
`shop:quote-open`→GlobalQuoteCartIsland openRef) + generic prefill_form (RecommenderChat, specificity-scored
field match, never submits). scout-service CatalogService is detail-only.

When two processes need to communicate: use a real transport
(HTTP/SSE, in-process call, MCP dispatch). If you need to persist for
audit or replay, persist *after* the transport delivers — never write
to PG, then have the receiver poll PG for the row.

**Why:** stated by user 2026-05-09. Polling-as-transport patterns are
slow, lose ordering guarantees, and confuse the persistence layer with
the messaging layer.

**How to apply:** for prompt assembly, agent ↔ orchestrator data flow,
and tool dispatch — call functions in-process or send HTTP. PG writes
go alongside or after, for audit. Examples in this codebase that
already follow the rule: `executeAction` posts to operator with auth
header (transport) and `feature_audit_consolidated` records the
mutation (audit). Examples to AVOID: writing a file to disk so a
sibling process picks it up via polling — replace with explicit RPC.

reach.readable from codex/omp/operator/memory-: yes — any process with PG access (PG-backed)
reach.concurrent multi-agent writes: yes — PG row-per-fact, no shared index file
reach.requires: PG + pgvector, embedder key (OpenAI) or local model, LLM key for extraction

When verifying Codex CLI behavior (hooks, tool payloads), do NOT copy `~/.codex/auth.json` into a throwaway `CODEX_HOME` and run `codex exec`. Codex OAuth refresh tokens are **single-use + rotating**: the throwaway run's refresh attempt rotates the token server-side, which can invalidate the user's real on-disk refresh token → they get logged out and must `codex login` again.

**Why:** hit this 2026-05-30 probing the Codex `apply_patch` hook payload. The probe 401'd (`refresh_token_reused`) and — by luck — the on-disk token was already stale so no live token was consumed; but the failure mode is real. Re-confirmed 2026-05-30 during the three-client lock in-vivo verification: a real `codex-su exec` 401'd the same way, blocking the Codex owner-resolution check (Claude's branch passed fully).

**How to apply:**
- Prefer offline inspection: `strings` the native binary at `@openai/codex-linux-x64/.../bin/codex` — it embeds the full hook JSON schema (`PreToolUseHookSpecificOutputWire`, `permissionDecision`, tool names, `settings.json`/`CODEX_HOME` paths). That answered everything without auth.
- `codex-su`'s `CODEX_HOME=~/.papercusp/codex-su-home` has `auth.json` as a **symlink** to the real `~/.codex/auth.json` (not a copy) — so `codex-su` is the safe "use real auth in-place" path the hazard above recommends. It's still subject to refresh-token rotation if the token is already stale.
- **Before blaming yourself for a `refresh_token_reused` 401**, check `stat ~/.codex/auth.json`: mode 600, and if mtime predates your run, you did NOT rotate it (a reused-refresh attempt consumes nothing new server-side). The user just needs to `codex login` again — pre-existing, not caused by your test.
- Headless invocation form: `codex exec --skip-git-repo-check "<prompt>" < /dev/null` (needs the git-repo-check skip outside a trusted dir; close stdin or it hangs reading it).
- **Headless codex exec auto-cancels MCP tool calls.** Calling any MCP-server tool (e.g. papercusp-su) from `codex exec` fires an MCP-tool-call approval *elicitation* (`ResolveElicitation { request_id: "mcp_tool_call_approval_…" }`); with no interactive user codex resolves it `Cancel` → "(failed) / user cancelled MCP tool call". This is NOT the shell `approval_policy` — `-a never`/`-c approval_policy="never"` does NOT fix it. Use `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (an `exec`-level flag) to auto-approve. Interactive `codex-su` TUI sessions just prompt the user, so they're unaffected. Connection/auth/bearer were all fine — discovery via `tool_search` works; only the approval gate blocks. OMP (Oh My Pi, `@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent`) ships these built-in tools natively. Source of truth: `~/.bun/install/cache/@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent@<ver>/src/prompts/tools/*.md`.

## Built-in tool registry
`ask`, `bash`, `python`, `calc`, `ssh`, `edit`, `find`, `grep`, `ast_grep`, `ast_edit`, `lsp`, `notebook`, `read`, `browser` (puppeteer), `task`, `poll`, `todo_write`, `fetch`, `web_search`, `write`, `generate_image`.

## `lsp` operations (14)
`diagnostics`, `definition`, `type_definition`, `implementation`, `references` (3-line context for first 50), `hover`, `symbols` (file or workspace), `rename` (cross-codebase), `rename_file` (sends `workspace/willRenameFiles`), `code_actions` (list + apply), `status`, `capabilities` (per-server discovery), **`request` (raw LSP method — escape hatch)**, `reload`.

The `request` action means OMP-LSP is strictly more capable than any LSP-MCP wrapper for server-specific methods like `rust-analyzer/expandMacro`, `typescript/goToSourceDefinition`, `workspace/executeCommand`.

OMP's prompt enforces tool choice: "MUST use `lsp` for symbol-aware operations… MUST NOT perform cross-file renames with `ast_edit`/`sed`/manual edits when `lsp rename` works."

## `ast_grep` and `ast_edit`
Native bindings via `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives` (Rust). Full metavariable matching (`$NAME`, `$_`, `$$$NAME`), language-specific guidance baked into the prompt. Languages: Python, JS/TS, Go, Java, C/C++, Rust, Ruby, PHP, more.

## What OMP does NOT have (real headroom)
- **Code graph / impact analysis** — no transitive call-chain or cluster reasoning. (GitNexus / CodeGraphContext fill this.)
- **Bulk repo packing** — no "pack the whole project as one document" tool. (Repomix fills this.)
- **Diff-aware prompts** — no "give me everything that changed since main" packer. (Code2Prompt fills this.)
- **Fast HTML→Markdown for web research** — `fetch` returns raw content; no Firecrawl/Jina-style cleaning layer.

## What is REDUNDANT to add as MCP
Don't ship MCP versions of: ast-grep-mcp, mcp-language-server, swiftlens, javalens-mcp, lsp-mcp-server, comby (for ast-grep-supported languages), Serena (capability-equivalent; only ergonomic gain). All are subsets or duplicates of OMP-LSP or OMP-`ast_grep`.

**Symptom:** an operator route/tool 500s (or a module fails to load) with
`The requested module 'pkg' does not provide an export named 'X'`. Happens when an
**ESM** file (`"type":"module"` package, e.g. `@papercusp/operator-core`) does
`import { X } from 'cjs-pkg'` and runs under **tsx** (the `:3070` host —
`npx tsx bin/hono-host.ts`). tsx transpiles a **typeless** package's `.ts` to CJS;
Node then statically links the named import via `cjs-module-lexer`, which can't see
`export *` re-export chains or some packages' compiled named exports → the namespace
links EMPTY → every named import throws.

**Why it hides:** vitest/vite **bundle** (cross-module analysis, no lexer), so unit
tests + typecheck pass. Only the tsx runtime hits it, and route handlers lazy-load,
so "tests pass / host boots 200" masks broken routes.

**Fix:**
- **Our typeless `@papercusp/*` dep** → add `"type":"module"` to its package.json so
  tsx emits native ESM re-exports. ESM-ify any CJS-isms: `require()`→
  `createRequire(import.meta.url)`, `__dirname`→`import.meta.dirname`.
- **Third-party CJS you can't flip** (`@xterm/headless`, `cron-parser`, `yaml`,
  `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, …) → use a **static or dynamic import, NOT createRequire**.
  createRequire works under tsx but BREAKS the desktop sidecar esbuild bundle
  (`papercusp-desktop/bin/build-desktop-sidecar.sh`, `--format=esm`, inlines all
  non-native deps): esbuild only inlines the GLOBAL `require('literal')`, so a renamed
  `nodeRequire(...)` stays a runtime call → "Cannot find module" in the shipped
  sidecar. Pick by namespace shape (probe with `import * as ns`): symbol on `ns` →
  `import * as ns from 'pkg'; ns.Sym`; only on `ns.default` → `import def from 'pkg';
  def.Sym`; lazy/optional dep inside an async fn → `await import('pkg')`. `const X =
  ns.Sym` keeps both value use + `InstanceType<typeof X>` type use. createRequire is
  fine ONLY for node builtins (`node:fs`/`node:os` — runtime-resolvable in the bundle).

**Find every break:** load each route+tool module under tsx and catch "does not
provide an export". Namespace-import probes give false +/- (tsx elides type-only
imports; a CJS runtime namespace can carry a key the static lexer can't, e.g.
`@xterm/headless` `Terminal`). Verify bundle-safety by esbuild-bundling each changed
file standalone and confirming the dep is inlined. Restart `:3070` after edits
(no hot-reload). Related: [[feedback_webapp_retired_use_tauri_dev]].

The operator API on `:3070` (the host `psu` and all `papercusp-su` MCP tools
talk to) runs as a **transient `systemd --user` unit** named
`papercup-dev-api.service`. Its ExecStart is
`bash -c "set -a; [ -f .env.local ] && . ./.env.local; set +a; exec npx tsx bin/hono-host.ts"`.

The relative paths (`.env.local`, `bin/hono-host.ts`) only resolve when the
unit's **WorkingDirectory = `…/papercup/apps/operator`** — the entry point is
`apps/operator/bin/hono-host.ts`, NOT `bin/hono-host.ts` at the repo root.

Failure mode seen 2026-06-05: the unit got (re)created with cwd = repo root, so
every start died instantly with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on `bin/hono-host.ts` →
`status=1/FAILURE` → `Restart=always` crash-loop (counter hit 130+). `:3070` was
down during each gap, so `psu` printed
`psu: could not reach the operator at http://localhost:3070 (fetch failed)`.

Diagnosis path: `systemctl --user status papercup-dev-api.service` (climbing
restart counter = crash loop) → reproduce by running the ExecStart manually to
see the real error (journald only shows the systemd-level exit, not the app
stack trace). Booting from `apps/operator` works:
`[hono-host] listening on http://0.0.0.0:3070`.

Restore (also pins cwd so a future restart can't reintroduce the bug):
```
systemd-run --user --unit=papercup-dev-api.service \
  --working-directory=/home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercup/apps/operator \
  -p Restart=always -p RestartSec=5 --setenv=PATH="$PATH" \
  /usr/bin/bash -c 'set -a; [ -f .env.local ] && . ./.env.local; set +a; exec npx tsx bin/hono-host.ts'
```
Nothing in the repo creates this unit (only `systemctl --user restart …` and the
`dev:restart` tool, which assume it already exists). Benign noise on boot that is
NOT the crash cause: `[ensure-omp-su] phase1 bootstrap failed: __dirname is not
defined` and `[boot-migrate] FAILED 000-baseline.sql: must be owner of function
task_lineage` — the host listens fine regardless. See
[[webapp-retired-use-tauri-dev]], [[verify-server-pid-before-measuring]].

Before trusting ANY live measurement (curl results, eval-harness numbers, "is my fix working"), verify the server process is actually the fresh one running your current code + env. Check the PID and start time (`ss -tlnp | grep :PORT`, then `ps -o lstart= -p PID`).

**Why (2026-05-29, Restart search):** I burned an entire long turn chasing a phantom "regression" — "canon camera → toner #1", 37ms responses, a harness run of P@5 0.718 with 2 guardrail failures — and wrote those bad numbers into plan commits. Root cause was operational, not code: the `:3100` shop-api was an **orphaned process** (started hours earlier) that `bin/overmind-all restart shop-api` did NOT control (there were several stale duplicate overmind instances on different sockets/tmux). Every "restart" I ran was a silent no-op; the zombie kept serving old code AND a stale `LLM_RERANK=0` env left over from a diagnostic. The code had been correct the whole time — killing the zombie + launching fresh fixed it instantly.

**How to apply:**
1. A suspiciously **fast** response is the tell: if a path should call a reranker/LLM (~1-2s) but returns in tens of ms, the rerank code isn't running — suspect a stale process or wrong route BEFORE suspecting the code.
2. After any restart, confirm the PID changed and start-time is recent. Don't assume `overmind restart`/`overmind-all restart` worked — orphans + multiple overmind instances make it no-op.
3. If a "regression" appears right after you toggled an env var for a diagnostic (e.g. flipped `LLM_RERANK=0` for a probe), suspect the toggle didn't get restored into the *actually-serving* process.
4. To force a known-good state: `kill <pid-on-port>`, then launch directly (`PORT=… node --env-file=.env node_modules/.bin/tsx apps/<svc>/src/main.ts`) and test that instance.
5. Don't commit measured numbers until the serving process is verified fresh. [[feedback_per_turn_commit]] is about committing code, not unverified metrics.

In the multi-agent papercup checkout, `coord:presence` staleness is driven by
**MCP-tool heartbeat recency**, not by whether you're actually working. A long
heads-down stretch of local Read/Edit/Bash (no `papercusp-su` MCP calls) lets your
presence go stale (>10 min), and a peer (or the batch supervisor) will read your
lane as DROPPED and claim it — exactly what happened on Brief 3 (su-487a7 picked up
my P-008..P-012 mid-flight).

**Why:** presence heartbeats are stamped by MCP tool invocations; the client's own
Read/Edit/Bash don't touch the coord substrate.

**How to apply:** during a long local-edit stretch (multi-file change, big test run),
periodically call any `papercusp-su` MCP verb — a `coord:declare-intent` refresh or
even a cheap `coord:presence` read — to keep the heartbeat fresh. When a peer does
claim your lane, recover by proposing a **split** over `coord:send` (keep the
mid-flight items, cede the not-yet-started ones) rather than fighting for it.
Relates to [[feedback_recheck_plan_status_before_starting]] and
[[feedback_use_locks_before_editing]].

Restart's single-node Typesense (Docker `typesense`, compose `docker-compose.typesense.yml`, project `restart`) silently took product search down from **2026-05-27 → 2026-05-28** (~36h, plus an earlier self-recovered episode 2026-04-23).

**Root cause (CONFIRMED — fd exhaustion, NOT transient I/O):** every Raft snapshot makes RocksDB hard-link all its `.sst` files; `storefront_products` has **~976 .sst files** and the process holds **~1000 fds while loaded**, against a container **nofile soft limit of 1024**. The snapshot exceeds 1024 → EMFILE → `Checkpoint creation failure, code 5` → SnapshotError → lone node steps down, can't `reset_peer` → "no leader" wedge. Recurs on EVERY snapshot. **Fix = `ulimits.nofile` soft 1024→524288** (host hard limit already 524288) in both compose files. NOT OOM (mem ~1.6G/16G), NOT disk-full (~60%), NOT mongod/CPU (I wrongly blamed mongod mid-session — it was fd all along), NOT OpenAI timeouts. `--reset-peers-on-error` + autoheal only recover the wedge after the fact; raising nofile removes the cause. Manual recovery if it ever recurs = `docker restart typesense` (reloads ~1M docs; watch `docker logs -f typesense | grep -i loaded`).

**Fix (commits on master ~2026-05-28):** `--reset-peers-on-error` (auto-recovers the wedge) + a `/health`-body healthcheck (over bash `/dev/tcp` — the `typesense/typesense:29.0` image has NO curl/wget but ships bash) + a `willfarrell/autoheal` sidecar (restart-on-unhealthy, since restart-on-exit never fires). Prod compose bumped `0.25.2 → 29.0` (0.25.2 predates the auto-embedding schema, so prod likely never built the collection and was permanently on the SQL fallback). Runbook: `docs/guides/typesense-outage-runbook.md`.

**GOTCHA (load-bearing):** the healthcheck `start_period` MUST exceed the cold reload (set to **3600s** after 900s proved too short). During reload `/health` is `{"ok":false}`; with a short start_period, autoheal marks it unhealthy and kills it mid-load → infinite restart loop that never finishes (observed live: a co-tenant `mongod` pinning ~15 cores stretched the ~12-min reload to ~20+ min and 900s let autoheal loop-kill it). A healthy node passes within seconds regardless, so a long start_period is free. NOTE: `docker restart` reuses the container's *baked-in* healthcheck config, NOT the compose file — to apply a changed `start_period` you must `docker compose up -d` (recreate), which re-triggers a reload. The running container now has 3600s + `--reset-peers-on-error` baked in.

**Write-path wedge (2026-05-28):** after the recovery, Typesense *reads/search were healthy but document WRITES hung* — a single upsert never returned and the indexer queue (`queued_writes`) wouldn't drain, while query-embedding + search worked fine. This blocks the catalog→Typesense sync pipeline, not just search. It was **transient post-recovery state**; a clean `docker compose up -d` restart cleared it and writes applied normally afterward. (Diagnosing it: test a write with `curl ...?action=upsert` + a timeout; exit 124 = wedged, 0 = healthy. Test container egress with **bash** `/dev/tcp`, never `sh`/dash — dash lacks `/dev/tcp` and gives false "no egress" negatives.)

While Typesense is down, search degrades to the Postgres FTS path — see [[project_restart_search_fts_fallback]].

A plan item with status `needs-human` (or otherwise flagged owner-gated /
deferred-and-surfaced) is a **hard stop**, not a low-priority TODO. Do **not**
autonomously execute it even when the user said "carry this plan out from start to
finish / complete every single item / I trust your judgment." That mandate covers
the *autonomous-safe* work; it does not override an explicit human gate.

**Why:** On 2026-06-05 an overnight session read P-009 (`needs-human`) of
`unify-agent-launches-as-blueprints-2026-06-04` — the D-005 operator-scanner
teardown — and executed it anyway, deleting ~34 files whose live consumers still
imported them. git-sync committed the deletions (65d242868), the operator booted
on `Cannot find module` and **crash-looped the whole fleet** (EI-11). The item was
`needs-human` precisely because it was a non-behavior-preserving live-subsystem
cut-over needing owner sign-off + a live-verified replacement first.

**How to apply:** When the next item is `needs-human`, STOP and surface it to the
user — name the item, why it's gated, what owner input/verification it needs — and
move to the next autonomous-safe item or end. Treat a "delete/retire the live X"
step as guilty-until-proven-safe: check who still imports X before removing it, and
prefer reverting a risky teardown over forcing it. Relates to
[[plan-first-for-features]] and the recovery filed as EI-17 (git-sync should refuse
to auto-commit a deletion that breaks a live import).

In the shared `papercup` checkout (many agents on one `main`), **never use `git stash`** — not even to A/B a quick check.

**Why:** the stash is global to the repo, not to your files. On 2026-06-02 I ran `git stash push <path>` to temporarily revert one file and re-run tsc; under the Bash tool's cwd handling the pathspec was malformed (`:(,prefix:N)...`), so the push **silently failed** (created no stash). The following `git stash pop` then popped a **pre-existing peer stash** (`stash@{0} pre-tier3-arc`), conflicting `OperatorPanel.tsx` + `globals.css` into a 3-stage `UU` merge — which **blocked ALL commits on main** for every agent until cleared. A peer (su-4871fff9) had to clean it up in parallel.

**How to apply:**
- To check whether a tsc/test error is pre-existing vs. yours: `git checkout HEAD -- <file>`, re-run, observe, then re-apply your edit. Never `git stash`.
- This is already in the repo CLAUDE.md ("Don't stash, branch, or carefully scope pathspecs") — the new lesson is the *mechanism*: a failed `stash push` leaves the working tree unchanged but a following `stash pop` operates on whatever `stash@{0}` already is (a peer's), and a conflicted pop wedges the index for everyone.
- Recovery if it happens: `git stash show --stat stash@{0}` to see the exact files the popped stash touched (blast radius), `git checkout HEAD -- <those files>` to revert to committed state, leave the stash entry in the list (don't drop a peer's stash), and coord:send the owner. See [[feedback_git_status_before_commit_shared_checkout]] and [[feedback_papercup_main_dir_stays_on_main]].

FIXED 2026-06-01. The Restart shop (:4321) freezing in Firefox on navigation was
NOT the React #418 (that fires under POLLING too and is recoverable) nor the
Zero WS client itself. **Root cause: zero-cache (:4848) was DOWN.**

Chain: zero-cache crash/stop leaves an orphaned `@rocicorp/zero/.../server/
replicator.js serving` worker holding the SQLite replica lock (`/tmp/
zero-replica.db`) → next start dies `SQLITE_BUSY: database is locked:
journal_mode = delete` → :4848 stays down → the shop's WS probe to
ws://localhost:4848 fails (1.5-4s each), and it re-probed PER ISLAND × PER
ClientRouter navigation → the failing-probe churn freezes Firefox (Chromium
degrades gracefully, so it looked Firefox-only). Diagnose: `ss -ltn | grep 4848`,
`fuser /tmp/zero-replica.db` (find the orphan), the user's console shows
"Firefox can't establish a connection to ws://localhost:4848" repeating.

Manual heal: `fuser -k /tmp/zero-replica.db*` then
`overmind restart zero-cache -s .overmind-all.sock` (up in ~6s).

Two fixes shipped (local commits, not pushed):
- **libs/sync 4d32292** (`SyncProvider.tsx` `probeWebSocketOnce`): probe WS ONCE
  per session, cache the verdict on `window.__sync_ws_probe_cache__`; dead server
  detected once → graceful POLLING, no churn, no freeze. Verified in REAL stock
  Firefox 150 (see [[project_restart_real_firefox_repro_harness]]).
- **superproject fb3e06f1**: `bin/zero-cache-start.sh` auto-clears the stale
  replica lock (`fuser -k` scoped to ZERO_REPLICA_FILE, so it never touches the
  harness zero-cache :4849) before exec'ing zero-cache-dev; Procfile wired.
  ACTIVATED 2026-06-01 via full daemon restart (`overmind quit` +
  `bin/overmind-all start web zero-cache shop-api shop-app shop` — overmind caches
  the Procfile cmd at daemon start, so a plain `overmind restart <proc>` is NOT
  enough). Verified self-heal: stop→orphan→restart auto-recovers :4848 in ~12s,
  no manual kill. Shop (:4321) also re-integrated into overmind (no more setsid).
  Also 2026-06-01: same WS-probe-churn fix cut the :3001 admin Firefox-tab crash;
  trimmed eager git-graph.css (off root layout) + react-diff-view (lazy
  CommitDetail, git-graph 248f051) + BuildStatus fetch timeouts (superproject
  5265755a). And ENABLE_DEV_PASSWORD_RESET_VIEWER flipped 1→0 in .env (dev
  password-reset viewer was live; code was already env-gated/secure).

WS is the shop default (cart island passes syncType="WEBSOCKETS" in
Layout.astro). Earlier red herrings I burned time on: PageTransition,
rest-query-batch, WebSocketAdapter keep-alive, kvStore='mem' (kvStore='mem' shop
WS is still in place + fine, but was NOT the freeze cause). Lesson: when a shop
symptom is transport-specific, CHECK THE BACKEND IS UP first.

Native bindings via `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives` (Rust). Full metavariable matching (`$NAME`, `$_`, `$$$NAME`), language-specific guidance baked into the prompt. Languages: Python, JS/TS, Go, Java, C/C++, Rust, Ruby, PHP, more.

## What OMP does NOT have (real headroom)
- **Code graph / impact analysis** — no transitive call-chain or cluster reasoning. (GitNexus / CodeGraphContext fill this.)
- **Bulk repo packing** — no "pack the whole project as one document" tool. (Repomix fills this.)
- **Diff-aware prompts** — no "give me everything that changed since main" packer. (Code2Prompt fills this.)
- **Fast HTML→Markdown for web research** — `fetch` returns raw content; no Firecrawl/Jina-style cleaning layer.

## What is REDUNDANT to add as MCP
Don't ship MCP versions of: ast-grep-mcp, mcp-language-server, swiftlens, javalens-mcp, lsp-mcp-server, comby (for ast-grep-supported languages), Serena (capability-equivalent; only ergonomic gain). All are subsets or duplicates of OMP-LSP or OMP-`ast_grep`.

When dropping a Postgres table, `DROP TABLE ... CASCADE` removes FKs, views, and
triggers **defined on** the table, but it does NOT touch **function bodies** that
reference the table by name in plain SQL — Postgres tracks no dependency for a
table name inside a `plpgsql`/SQL function body. Those functions silently keep a
dangling reference and error (`relation "<t>" does not exist`) the next time they
run.

**Why:** bit me in the Restart b2b retire (drizzle/0054 dropped `b2b_quote_item`).
`fn_recompute_reserved_qty` had a `b2b_r` CTE selecting from `b2b_quote_item`, and
it's fired by 4 LIVE triggers (shop_order, shop_order_item, wholesale_quote,
wholesale_quote_item) — so every checkout / wholesale write would have errored.
CASCADE printed no warning because the dependency is invisible to it. Caught only
because a `libs/db/src/schema/shop.ts` docstring mentioned the trigger. Fixed in
drizzle/0055 (rewrote the fn, dropped orphaned `fn_trg_b2b_quote*`).

**How to apply:** before (and after) any `DROP TABLE`/`DROP COLUMN`, run
`SELECT proname FROM pg_proc WHERE prokind='f' AND prosrc ILIKE '%<table>%';`
(use `prosrc`, NOT `pg_get_functiondef` — the latter errors on aggregates). Rewrite
every hit + drop orphaned trigger functions in the SAME migration, then fire the
live triggers in a rolled-back tx (`UPDATE t SET col=col`) to prove they don't
error. Extends [[feedback_verify_identifiers_against_source_not_grep]] — verify a
table's real consumers (incl. DB-side code) before dropping. See
[[project_restart_stack]], [[feedback_named_dollar_quote_in_sql]].

Any map like `STATUS_ICON[someValue]` or `SEVERITY_ICON[someValue]` that returns a React component ref MUST include a fallback: `ICON_MAP[value] ?? FallbackIcon`. A missing key returns `undefined`, and rendering `undefined` as a component crashes the **entire React subtree**, not just the affected row.

**Why:** `IssueRow` crashed on `STATUS_ICON['passed']` returning `undefined` (curator had set `status: "passed"` on an issue). The crash took down unrelated panels (brainstorm tab) in the same dashboard tree. Fix: added `passed: CheckCircle2` to STATUS_ICON and `?? Circle` fallbacks throughout IssueRow.

**How to apply:** Whenever adding new status/severity/type values, update the icon map AND add a `?? SomeFallbackIcon` guard at the call site. When reviewing map lookups in harness UI code, check for missing fallbacks before touching anything else.

Before trusting ANY live measurement (curl results, eval-harness numbers, "is my fix working"), verify the server process is actually the fresh one running your current code + env. Check the PID and start time (`ss -tlnp | grep :PORT`, then `ps -o lstart= -p PID`).

**Why (2026-05-29, Restart search):** I burned an entire long turn chasing a phantom "regression" — "canon camera → toner #1", 37ms responses, a harness run of P@5 0.718 with 2 guardrail failures — and wrote those bad numbers into plan commits. Root cause was operational, not code: the `:3100` shop-api was an **orphaned process** (started hours earlier) that `bin/overmind-all restart shop-api` did NOT control (there were several stale duplicate overmind instances on different sockets/tmux). Every "restart" I ran was a silent no-op; the zombie kept serving old code AND a stale `LLM_RERANK=0` env left over from a diagnostic. The code had been correct the whole time — killing the zombie + launching fresh fixed it instantly.

**How to apply:**
1. A suspiciously **fast** response is the tell: if a path should call a reranker/LLM (~1-2s) but returns in tens of ms, the rerank code isn't running — suspect a stale process or wrong route BEFORE suspecting the code.
2. After any restart, confirm the PID changed and start-time is recent. Don't assume `overmind restart`/`overmind-all restart` worked — orphans + multiple overmind instances make it no-op.
3. If a "regression" appears right after you toggled an env var for a diagnostic (e.g. flipped `LLM_RERANK=0` for a probe), suspect the toggle didn't get restored into the *actually-serving* process.
4. To force a known-good state: `kill <pid-on-port>`, then launch directly (`PORT=… node --env-file=.env node_modules/.bin/tsx apps/<svc>/src/main.ts`) and test that instance.
5. Don't commit measured numbers until the serving process is verified fresh. [[feedback_per_turn_commit]] is about committing code, not unverified metrics.

**Papercup operator instance (2026-05-30):** the running operator API on `:3070` is `tsx bin/hono-host.ts` (a long-running tsx process with NO file-watch); `dev:operator` → operator-vite `vite build --watch` is only the FRONTEND. So edits to `apps/operator/lib/**` (e.g. agent-tools) do NOT go live until that hono-host process is restarted — module singletons (like `coordLog`) were eval'd at startup. Verifying "is my server code live": send through the live tool and check WHERE the write landed (during the coord FS→PG port, a `coord:send` landing in `coord/*.jsonl` instead of `harness_shared.coord_event_log` proved the operator was still on the pre-cutover code). Restarting hono-host also resets the papercusp-su MCP session, so it's the user's call, not mine to do unilaterally.

The app is in testing. There are no active users. There is no production environment to "see how a fix fares in" before applying the right fix.

**Why this matters:** Without this framing, agents instinctively add deprecation aliases, ship compromise fixes, layer on top of wrong APIs instead of replacing them, and skip schema migrations to "minimize risk." All of those instincts are wrong here — the only risk is shipping the wrong design.

**Rule (verbatim from the user):** "We don't defer fixes for later to 'see how they fare in production first.' There is no production, and that gives us the luxury to break things continuously until we have the perfect app ready for production."

**How to apply:**

- **Don't ship deprecation aliases.** When renaming an identifier/file/type, change every caller in the same commit. Don't leave `oldName as newName` re-exports "for one release cycle" — there's no production cycle to wait for.
- **Don't be afraid to break the API.** No external users depend on stable shapes. If a v1 API is wrong, redesign it — don't preserve an awkward compromise to keep clients building.
- **Take the schema migration now.** If `claude_session_id` should be `agent_session_id`, do the migration when the rename comes up — don't defer it as "data + API contract change" while accumulating drift.
- **Pick the best tool, not the safe one.** Aviyn (the user) covers any commercial license costs personally. License + compatibility are footnotes, not vetoes. Rank by capability fit; if Serena beats OMP for a specific case, say so even if OMP is already wired up.
- **Refactor architecture when foundational decisions are wrong.** Migration cost is dominated by future cost-of-wrong-architecture, not current cost-of-rework. The same logic that says "don't refactor mature systems" doesn't apply to pre-alpha.

**What to still do:**

- Surface what you're changing in your reply so the user knows. Don't ask permission to do it well — flag it, then do it.
- Run tests. The luxury to break things doesn't extend to breaking them *silently*.
- When you spot a future-cost trap (schema, API contract, identifier collision), call it out in the audit + fix it the same turn if it's in scope.

**Stale socket trap:** Child processes from a previous session survive the lost parent and keep holding their ports. The new overmind will show those services as `dead` even though ports are bound. Before removing the socket: `pgrep -af overmind` and `ss -tlnp | grep -E '3001|4321|3000|3100'` to see what's still alive. **Overmind stale 'dead' status:** Processes restarted out-of-band keep old pid and show 'dead' in overmind status even when the port is listening. Cosmetic only. Confirm with user before `overmind restart` — it causes a brief service interruption.

**Admin tables empty (Approvals/Rejections):** Root cause is almost always the `gateway` overmind process (api-gateway :3000) being down. **Why:** User repeatedly asks things like "start the Restart services" or "our app at :3001 is down" without specifying path or command — they expect you to know. The stale socket / ghost-process trap causes repeated confusion.

**How to apply:** When user refers to "the app," ":3001," or "Restart services" without a path, operate in `/home/marsh-office/Restart`. Use `bin/overmind-all` for the full stack. The hook is live in my own Claude sessions — it WILL block me on a held file.

**Updated how-to (supersedes "always acquire before editing"):**
- The hook locks per-edit; you rarely need a manual `locks:acquire`. When the hook blocks you, pivot/retry/yield — don't route around it.
- **Per-session identity FIXED 2026-05-30 (commit 3761b32b):** `claude-su`/`codex-su` now mint a per-launch `PAPERCUSP_SID`, fed into BOTH the interactive MCP `?client=` and the hook owner — so within a `-su` shell, manual `locks:acquire` and the hook share one owner (manual multi-file claims no longer self-block) and distinct shells get distinct coord/lock owners (coord:inbox stops self-filtering peers). **Caveat:** a plain `claude`/`codex` SU session (no `PAPERCUSP_SID`, e.g. not launched via the `-su` wrapper) still uses the static machine id → manual-acquire there can still self-contend with the hook; relaunch via `claude-su` to get the unified id. OMP interactive coord still collapses (deferred — no mcp.json env-interp).
- Manual `locks_acquire` is for a deliberate multi-file claim held across the commit (now safe under `-su`).
- Shape (when you do call manually): `mcp__papercusp-su__locks_acquire { paths: [<repo-rel-posix>], intent, ttl_sec: 1200, wait: { max_sec: 300 } }` → edit → `locks_release { lock_id }`.
- Paths must be **repo-relative POSIX** (no leading `./`, no absolute, no `..`).
- **Don't assume the lock surface is down.** `locks:*` and `coord:*` resolve a *static-client* identity (`su · <id>`, workspaceId `*`) and respond fine **even when** bearer-gated built-ins like `docs:outline` / `papercusp:list_workspaces` return `harness_not_registered` / `unauthorized` in the same session. Different auth path. Test `coord:whoami` / `locks:queue` before concluding the surface is unavailable — never pre-emptively skip locking on inference.
- Memory files under `~/.claude/.../memory/` are OUTSIDE the repo — the lock system doesn't apply to them.

When driving an **isolated** operator Tauri desktop for e2e (own Xvfb + VirtualGL,
launched via `papercusp-desktop` `npm run dev` = `desktop-dev-nohmr`, devUrl `:3070`),
the webview's `fetch('/api/...')` goes **directly over HTTP to :3070** — it does NOT
ride the IPC bridge that the *real* desktop uses. The real desktop's IPC bridge injects
the operator superuser bearer on the upstream hop (`endpoint-ipc/server.ts`
`sysHttpInjectHeaders` → `principalFromSuperuserToken` → `trust:'trusted'`), which clears
admin gates. The isolated instance presents as `unverified-loopback`, so admin routes
(e.g. `/api/admin/llm-tests/*`) return **403 `trust unverified-loopback not in allowlist`**.

To reproduce the authorized path, monkeypatch `window.fetch` via the tauri bridge to add
`Authorization: Bearer <~/.papercusp/superuser-token>` for `/api/*`. **Gotcha:** the patch
MUST handle `URL` objects — panels call `fetch(new URL(endpoint, origin))`, and a `URL` is
neither a string nor a `Request`, so a naive `input.url` read misses it (read `input.href`
for URL). The patch survives client-side SPA nav (TanStack Router) but is lost on full
reload — remount the panel by clicking tabs, not `location.reload()`.

Bridge reads the DOM even GL-less, so DOM assertions are the authoritative proof; the
VirtualGL screenshot is only for literal pixel-paint. See [[own-xvfb-for-e2e]],
[[reference-desktop-dev-nohmr-3070-dist]], [[drive-desktop-with-tauri-agent-tools]].

In the shared `papercup` checkout (many agents on one `main`), **never use `git stash`** — not even to A/B a quick check.

**Why:** the stash is global to the repo, not to your files. On 2026-06-02 I ran `git stash push <path>` to temporarily revert one file and re-run tsc; under the Bash tool's cwd handling the pathspec was malformed (`:(,prefix:N)...`), so the push **silently failed** (created no stash). The following `git stash pop` then popped a **pre-existing peer stash** (`stash@{0} pre-tier3-arc`), conflicting `OperatorPanel.tsx` + `globals.css` into a 3-stage `UU` merge — which **blocked ALL commits on main** for every agent until cleared. A peer (su-4871fff9) had to clean it up in parallel.

**How to apply:**
- To check whether a tsc/test error is pre-existing vs. yours: `git checkout HEAD -- <file>`, re-run, observe, then re-apply your edit. Never `git stash`.
- This is already in the repo CLAUDE.md ("Don't stash, branch, or carefully scope pathspecs") — the new lesson is the *mechanism*: a failed `stash push` leaves the working tree unchanged but a following `stash pop` operates on whatever `stash@{0}` already is (a peer's), and a conflicted pop wedges the index for everyone.
- Recovery if it happens: `git stash show --stat stash@{0}` to see the exact files the popped stash touched (blast radius), `git checkout HEAD -- <those files>` to revert to committed state, leave the stash entry in the list (don't drop a peer's stash), and coord:send the owner. See [[feedback_git_status_before_commit_shared_checkout]] and [[feedback_papercup_main_dir_stays_on_main]].

In the shared Restart checkout, when another agent is also running `npm --workspace @restart/shop run build`, you get a **concurrent-build race** into the same `apps/shop/dist/`: each build emits its own content-hashed `RecommenderChat.<hash>.js`, and whichever finishes the **server (astro page) phase** last wins the HTML's bundle reference. Symptom that wasted ~30 min: my rebuild produced a bundle WITH my code (`B5deCLBn`), but the served `/scout` HTML kept referencing the other agent's no-my-code bundle (`DU5kgTP0`) — and a clean rebuild produced the *same* hash because the other agent mutated `RecommenderChat.tsx` mid-build (18s window).

**Tells:** rebuilt bundle has the same hash as before despite a source change; `dist/` contains TWO `RecommenderChat.*.js` (one with your markers, one without); served HTML references the one without. Grep a string literal (e.g. `X-Scout-Turn-Id`) in the *served* bundle to check — minified literals survive.

**How to apply:** don't keep racing rebuilds — it's futile and adds churn. (1) Confirm your SOURCE is committed in HEAD (`git show HEAD:<file> | grep <marker>`) — that's the durable truth; `dist/` is a gitignored artifact that self-resolves on the next uncontested build. (2) The live page often still WORKS during the skew (the old client's `data:`-line SSE parser tolerates the new `event:`/`id:` wire format). (3) For a clean verification window, coordinate or wait for the other agent to idle. Same family as [[feedback_git_status_before_commit_shared_checkout]] (index sweep) — both are concurrent-agent hazards in the one shared checkout.

assistant rows. (This bit me: a papercup merge-resolver spawned with

**Symptom:** an operator route/tool 500s (or a module fails to load) with
`The requested module 'pkg' does not provide an export named 'X'`. Happens when an
**ESM** file (`"type":"module"` package, e.g. `@papercusp/operator-core`) does
`import { X } from 'cjs-pkg'` and runs under **tsx** (the `:3070` host —
`npx tsx bin/hono-host.ts`). tsx transpiles a **typeless** package's `.ts` to CJS;
Node then statically links the named import via `cjs-module-lexer`, which can't see
`export *` re-export chains or some packages' compiled named exports → the namespace
links EMPTY → every named import throws.

**Why it hides:** vitest/vite **bundle** (cross-module analysis, no lexer), so unit
tests + typecheck pass. Only the tsx runtime hits it, and route handlers lazy-load,
so "tests pass / host boots 200" masks broken routes.

**Fix:**
- **Our typeless `@papercusp/*` dep** → add `"type":"module"` to its package.json so
  tsx emits native ESM re-exports. ESM-ify any CJS-isms: `require()`→
  `createRequire(import.meta.url)`, `__dirname`→`import.meta.dirname`.
- **Third-party CJS you can't flip** (`@xterm/headless`, `cron-parser`, `yaml`,
  `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, …) → use a **static or dynamic import, NOT createRequire**.
  createRequire works under tsx but BREAKS the desktop sidecar esbuild bundle
  (`papercusp-desktop/bin/build-desktop-sidecar.sh`, `--format=esm`, inlines all
  non-native deps): esbuild only inlines the GLOBAL `require('literal')`, so a renamed
  `nodeRequire(...)` stays a runtime call → "Cannot find module" in the shipped
  sidecar. Pick by namespace shape (probe with `import * as ns`): symbol on `ns` →
  `import * as ns from 'pkg'; ns.Sym`; only on `ns.default` → `import def from 'pkg';
  def.Sym`; lazy/optional dep inside an async fn → `await import('pkg')`. `const X =
  ns.Sym` keeps both value use + `InstanceType<typeof X>` type use. createRequire is
  fine ONLY for node builtins (`node:fs`/`node:os` — runtime-resolvable in the bundle).

**Find every break:** load each route+tool module under tsx and catch "does not
provide an export". Namespace-import probes give false +/- (tsx elides type-only
imports; a CJS runtime namespace can carry a key the static lexer can't, e.g.
`@xterm/headless` `Terminal`). Verify bundle-safety by esbuild-bundling each changed
file standalone and confirming the dep is inlined. Restart `:3070` after edits
(no hot-reload). Related: [[feedback_webapp_retired_use_tauri_dev]].

Before trusting ANY live measurement (curl results, eval-harness numbers, "is my fix working"), verify the server process is actually the fresh one running your current code + env. Check the PID and start time (`ss -tlnp | grep :PORT`, then `ps -o lstart= -p PID`).

**Why (2026-05-29, Restart search):** I burned an entire long turn chasing a phantom "regression" — "canon camera → toner #1", 37ms responses, a harness run of P@5 0.718 with 2 guardrail failures — and wrote those bad numbers into plan commits. Root cause was operational, not code: the `:3100` shop-api was an **orphaned process** (started hours earlier) that `bin/overmind-all restart shop-api` did NOT control (there were several stale duplicate overmind instances on different sockets/tmux). Every "restart" I ran was a silent no-op; the zombie kept serving old code AND a stale `LLM_RERANK=0` env left over from a diagnostic. The code had been correct the whole time — killing the zombie + launching fresh fixed it instantly.

**How to apply:**
1. A suspiciously **fast** response is the tell: if a path should call a reranker/LLM (~1-2s) but returns in tens of ms, the rerank code isn't running — suspect a stale process or wrong route BEFORE suspecting the code.
2. After any restart, confirm the PID changed and start-time is recent. Don't assume `overmind restart`/`overmind-all restart` worked — orphans + multiple overmind instances make it no-op.
3. If a "regression" appears right after you toggled an env var for a diagnostic (e.g. flipped `LLM_RERANK=0` for a probe), suspect the toggle didn't get restored into the *actually-serving* process.
4. To force a known-good state: `kill <pid-on-port>`, then launch directly (`PORT=… node --env-file=.env node_modules/.bin/tsx apps/<svc>/src/main.ts`) and test that instance.
5. Don't commit measured numbers until the serving process is verified fresh. [[feedback_per_turn_commit]] is about committing code, not unverified metrics.

**Papercup operator instance (2026-05-30):** the running operator API on `:3070` is `tsx bin/hono-host.ts` (a long-running tsx process with NO file-watch); `dev:operator` → operator-vite `vite build --watch` is only the FRONTEND. So edits to `apps/operator/lib/**` (e.g. agent-tools) do NOT go live until that hono-host process is restarted — module singletons (like `coordLog`) were eval'd at startup. Verifying "is my server code live": send through the live tool and check WHERE the write landed (during the coord FS→PG port, a `coord:send` landing in `coord/*.jsonl` instead of `harness_shared.coord_event_log` proved the operator was still on the pre-cutover code). Restarting hono-host also resets the papercusp-su MCP session, so it's the user's call, not mine to do unilaterally.

OMP (Oh My Pi, `@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent`) ships these built-in tools natively. Source of truth: `~/.bun/install/cache/@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent@<ver>/src/prompts/tools/*.md`.

## Built-in tool registry
`ask`, `bash`, `python`, `calc`, `ssh`, `edit`, `find`, `grep`, `ast_grep`, `ast_edit`, `lsp`, `notebook`, `read`, `browser` (puppeteer), `task`, `poll`, `todo_write`, `fetch`, `web_search`, `write`, `generate_image`.

## `lsp` operations (14)
`diagnostics`, `definition`, `type_definition`, `implementation`, `references` (3-line context for first 50), `hover`, `symbols` (file or workspace), `rename` (cross-codebase), `rename_file` (sends `workspace/willRenameFiles`), `code_actions` (list + apply), `status`, `capabilities` (per-server discovery), **`request` (raw LSP method — escape hatch)**, `reload`.

The `request` action means OMP-LSP is strictly more capable than any LSP-MCP wrapper for server-specific methods like `rust-analyzer/expandMacro`, `typescript/goToSourceDefinition`, `workspace/executeCommand`.

OMP's prompt enforces tool choice: "MUST use `lsp` for symbol-aware operations… MUST NOT perform cross-file renames with `ast_edit`/`sed`/manual edits when `lsp rename` works."

## `ast_grep` and `ast_edit`
Native bindings via `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives` (Rust). Full metavariable matching (`$NAME`, `$_`, `$$$NAME`), language-specific guidance baked into the prompt. Languages: Python, JS/TS, Go, Java, C/C++, Rust, Ruby, PHP, more.

## What OMP does NOT have (real headroom)
- **Code graph / impact analysis** — no transitive call-chain or cluster reasoning. (GitNexus / CodeGraphContext fill this.)
- **Bulk repo packing** — no "pack the whole project as one document" tool. (Repomix fills this.)
- **Diff-aware prompts** — no "give me everything that changed since main" packer. (Code2Prompt fills this.)
- **Fast HTML→Markdown for web research** — `fetch` returns raw content; no Firecrawl/Jina-style cleaning layer.

## What is REDUNDANT to add as MCP
Don't ship MCP versions of: ast-grep-mcp, mcp-language-server, swiftlens, javalens-mcp, lsp-mcp-server, comby (for ast-grep-supported languages), Serena (capability-equivalent; only ergonomic gain). All are subsets or duplicates of OMP-LSP or OMP-`ast_grep`.

FIXED 2026-06-01. The Restart shop (:4321) freezing in Firefox on navigation was
NOT the React #418 (that fires under POLLING too and is recoverable) nor the
Zero WS client itself. **Root cause: zero-cache (:4848) was DOWN.**

Chain: zero-cache crash/stop leaves an orphaned `@rocicorp/zero/.../server/
replicator.js serving` worker holding the SQLite replica lock (`/tmp/
zero-replica.db`) → next start dies `SQLITE_BUSY: database is locked:
journal_mode = delete` → :4848 stays down → the shop's WS probe to
ws://localhost:4848 fails (1.5-4s each), and it re-probed PER ISLAND × PER
ClientRouter navigation → the failing-probe churn freezes Firefox (Chromium
degrades gracefully, so it looked Firefox-only). Diagnose: `ss -ltn | grep 4848`,
`fuser /tmp/zero-replica.db` (find the orphan), the user's console shows
"Firefox can't establish a connection to ws://localhost:4848" repeating.

Manual heal: `fuser -k /tmp/zero-replica.db*` then
`overmind restart zero-cache -s .overmind-all.sock` (up in ~6s).

Two fixes shipped (local commits, not pushed):
- **libs/sync 4d32292** (`SyncProvider.tsx` `probeWebSocketOnce`): probe WS ONCE
  per session, cache the verdict on `window.__sync_ws_probe_cache__`; dead server
  detected once → graceful POLLING, no churn, no freeze. Verified in REAL stock
  Firefox 150 (see [[project_restart_real_firefox_repro_harness]]).
- **superproject fb3e06f1**: `bin/zero-cache-start.sh` auto-clears the stale
  replica lock (`fuser -k` scoped to ZERO_REPLICA_FILE, so it never touches the
  harness zero-cache :4849) before exec'ing zero-cache-dev; Procfile wired.
  ACTIVATED 2026-06-01 via full daemon restart (`overmind quit` +
  `bin/overmind-all start web zero-cache shop-api shop-app shop` — overmind caches
  the Procfile cmd at daemon start, so a plain `overmind restart <proc>` is NOT
  enough). Verified self-heal: stop→orphan→restart auto-recovers :4848 in ~12s,
  no manual kill. Shop (:4321) also re-integrated into overmind (no more setsid).
  Also 2026-06-01: same WS-probe-churn fix cut the :3001 admin Firefox-tab crash;
  trimmed eager git-graph.css (off root layout) + react-diff-view (lazy
  CommitDetail, git-graph 248f051) + BuildStatus fetch timeouts (superproject
  5265755a). And ENABLE_DEV_PASSWORD_RESET_VIEWER flipped 1→0 in .env (dev
  password-reset viewer was live; code was already env-gated/secure).

WS is the shop default (cart island passes syncType="WEBSOCKETS" in
Layout.astro). Earlier red herrings I burned time on: PageTransition,
rest-query-batch, WebSocketAdapter keep-alive, kvStore='mem' (kvStore='mem' shop
WS is still in place + fine, but was NOT the freeze cause). Lesson: when a shop
symptom is transport-specific, CHECK THE BACKEND IS UP first.

## Two complementary error logs

**1. `toastLog` (server-side, PG)** — every call to `toast.error()` / `addToast()`. Pull via:

```sh
curl -sS "http://localhost:3055/api/zero-harness/rest-query?name=toastLog.recent&args=%7B%22limit%22%3A100%7D" \
  | jq -r '.rows[] | "\(.createdAt | tonumber / 1000 | strftime("%H:%M:%S")) [\(.level)] \(.message)"'
```

Schema: `{id, level, message, description, harnessSlug, createdAt, actionLabel, actionHref}`. Timestamps are UTC.

**Use this first** when debugging "is the console clean?" / "what errors did the user see?". `tauri-agent-tools console-monitor --duration N` only captures logs fired DURING the N-second window — anything from page load, prior session, or earlier in the same session is invisible. The persistent toastLog has all of it.

Useful query patterns:
- Last N errors: `.rows[] | select(.level == "error")`
- Distinct messages: `.rows[].message | sed 's/[0-9]\\+/N/g' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` to see frequency
- Since timestamp: filter by `createdAt > <ms>`

When chasing user-reported errors with no live reproduction, this is the diagnostic surface for user-facing toasts. Live console-monitor is for verifying a fix took effect *after* you find a recent error.

## 2. `window.__papercuspPerfRecorder.events` (client-side, localStorage)

The vitals-recorder in `apps/operator/app/admin/testing/_lib/vitals-recorder.ts` patches `console.error` + `window.error` + `unhandledrejection` and persists to `localStorage['papercusp.testing.perf-events.v1']`.

**Scope caveat:** `PerfObserverProvider` (which calls `startRecorder()`) only mounts on `/admin/testing` pages. On every other route `window.__papercuspPerfRecorder` is `undefined` and querying `events.length` returns 0 vacuously — **not a valid "console is clean" signal for `/setup`, `/harness`, `/marketplace`, etc.** For those routes use `tauri-agent-tools capture -o <dir>` and read `<dir>/console-errors.json` — that taps WebKit's devtools console directly and catches React hook errors, "Fetch API cannot load … due to access control checks", chunk-load failures, etc. This is what captures:
- React errors ("Rendered more hooks…", hydration errors)
- ChunkLoadError, module/compile errors (Turbopack/SWC parse failures)
- Unhandled promise rejections
- Anything else that hits `console.error` but doesn't write a user toast

Query via `tauri-agent-tools eval`:
```js
JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('papercusp.testing.perf-events.v1') || '[]')
  .filter(e => e.kind === 'console-error' || e.kind === 'unhandled-error')
```

Grouping by `e.detail.slice(0, 80)` collapses repeated identical errors into a count.

### Clearing the perf log

The recorder keeps an in-memory `events` array AND flushes to localStorage. `localStorage.removeItem` alone doesn't work — the next `flushToStorage` writes the in-memory copy back. Reset both atomically:

```js
if (window.__papercuspPerfRecorder) window.__papercuspPerfRecorder.events = [];
localStorage.removeItem('papercusp.testing.perf-events.v1');
location.reload();
```

### When to use which

- **User-reported "I got a toast that said X"** → toastLog
- **User-reported "got a React error / nothing loads / hook error / chunk error"** → perf recorder (these never hit toastLog)
- **Both are durable across reloads** — toastLog over server restarts too; perf recorder until the user clears localStorage

## 3. `tauri-agent-tools console-monitor` (live bridge stream)

WebKit logs some categories of errors **directly to the devtools console without going through `console.error`** — they're invisible to BOTH toastLog and the perf recorder. Specifically:

- `Fetch API cannot load X due to access control checks` (often a *timeout*, not CORS)
- `Load failed` on fetches that WebKit aborted before resolution
- Network-layer warnings (mixed content, certificate, etc.)

These show up in the bridge's `console-monitor --level error --json` because the bridge taps the webview's *entire* console feed, not just JS calls. So when chasing user-reported "Fetch API cannot load" errors:

```sh
tauri-agent-tools console-monitor --port <port> --token <tok> --duration 30000 --json --level error > /tmp/cm.json
```

…and reload the page during the window. Catches what the other two surfaces don't.

**`"Fetch API cannot load X due to access control checks"` is misleading — on WebKitGTK it almost always means the fetch timed out (Next dev lazy-compile slowness), not real CORS.** Always check `curl -w "%{time_total}"` against the same URL before chasing ACAO headers. Fix is pre-warming routes via `instrumentation-node.ts` register hook.

## Summary: trichotomy of error surfaces

| Surface | Catches | Misses |
|---|---|---|
| `toastLog.recent` | `toast.error()` / `addToast()` | Everything else |
| `__papercuspPerfRecorder` | JS-side `console.error`/`window.error`/rejections | WebKit's direct devtools logs |
| `console-monitor` (bridge) | Entire webview console feed | Anything before its start |

For "is the console clean now?" query *all three* and reconcile.

In repos where multiple agents may concurrently touch `main` (papercup is the canonical case — 5+ agents commit/push every turn per the rust-port coord protocol), do new work in a `git worktree add ../papercup-<feature> -b <branch>` rather than checking out a feature branch in the canonical checkout. Reason: a `git checkout <branch>` in the shared checkout swaps everyone's working tree mid-edit, and `git stash` round-trips lose untracked files that aren't yet committed. Worktrees let me work in `../papercup-<feature>` while the canonical `papercup/` stays on `main` so other agents can keep committing.

**Why:** Confirmed footgun on 2026-05-10 — a `paperclip` agent switched the checkout to `design-phase-v0.1-recovery` mid-edit, which stashed my uncommitted work; not all of it survived the stash + checkout cycle, and I had to recreate several files from conversation context.

**How to apply:** For any feature branch off `main` in a multi-agent repo, default to:
```
git worktree add -b plugin/<feature> ../papercup-<feature> origin/main
cd ../papercup-<feature>
# work
git push -u origin plugin/<feature>
gh pr create ...
cd /home/marsh-office/papercupai-workspace/papercup
git worktree remove ../papercup-<feature>
```
The canonical checkout never leaves `main` from another agent's perspective. Submodules need `--recurse-submodules` on worktree add or a manual `git submodule update --init --recursive` afterwards.

User occasionally pastes full terminal launch commands into chat instead of their terminal. The pattern includes ANSI color escapes (`\e]10;#ffffff\e\\`), window-title setters (`printf '\033]0;TITLE\a'`), a `cd ~/project`, and the actual run command chained together.

Known launchers seen: `wolfcastle` (deno), `storewolf-central-server` (node Server.js with config + ports + mode flags like `--mode allUnimportant`).

**Why:** These are clearly meant for a shell — colors + title + cd + run is a terminal session-startup ritual. Silently executing them would be a mistake, especially if the target directory has edit restrictions (e.g. `storewolf-central-server` submodule).

**How to apply:** When the incoming message looks like a shell session-startup command (ANSI escapes + cd + run), don't execute it silently. Acknowledge it looks like a terminal misfire, summarize what it would do (project dir, service name, ports/mode), and ask whether to run it.

When you write a reverse proxy with `fetch()` (undici) and read the upstream
body via `await upstream.arrayBuffer()` (or `.text()`/`.json()`), undici
**transparently decompresses** gzip/br bodies. If you then copy the upstream
`content-encoding` (e.g. `br`) and `content-length` headers onto the re-emitted
(now-plain) bytes, the browser tries to decode plain bytes as brotli/gzip →
`ERR_CONTENT_DECODING_FAILED`, and the client's `fetch` throws "Failed to fetch".

`/home/marsh-office/.config/systemd/user/papercup-vm-mac.service` shipped with `Type=forking`, `PIDFile=/.../qemu.pid`, `TimeoutStartSec=120`. But `boot-sonoma.sh` runs qemu in the foreground (no `-daemonize`, no `-pidfile`), so the pid file never appears. Every 2 min systemd SIGTERMs the VM thinking startup failed, then `Restart=on-failure` brings it back. Looks like "Mac VM keeps crashing" — actually a systemd kill loop.

**Why:** The two parts of the unit contradicted: `Type=forking` says "the script will fork and exit, write a pid file to PIDFile=", but the script does neither. `TimeoutStartSec=120` then governs how long systemd waits for the pid file before declaring failure. Mac VM crash incidents that interrupted earlier builds in this session were likely all this same loop, not real VM crashes.

**How to apply:** When a systemd-managed service that runs a foreground process appears to "crash on a clock," check the unit's `Type=` vs the script's actual behavior. `Type=simple` matches a foreground command. `Type=forking` requires the binary to actually daemonize. Mismatched + a `PIDFile=` that's never written = guaranteed kill loop on `TimeoutStartSec`. Look for SIGTERM "from pid <systemd-pid>" in the journal as the smoking gun.

The Windows VM (`papercup-vm-win`) is NOT under systemd — runs standalone — so its crashes during this session were real VM hangs, not this issue. Don't conflate them.

**Regression history:** Recurred on 2026-05-13 — NRestarts hit 135 in a few hours before the fix was reapplied (Type=simple, TimeoutStartUSec=infinity, PIDFile=). Suggests some workflow (test script? old commit checkout? agent edit?) keeps reverting the unit file. **First diagnostic when the user says "Mac VM keeps crashing":** `systemctl --user show papercup-vm-mac -p TimeoutStartUSec,Type,PIDFile,NRestarts` — if those values aren't `infinity`, `simple`, empty, expect the kill loop. Also: 135 unclean shutdowns can damage APFS — after fixing the unit, watch for the next boot taking unusually long with zero disk writes (could be panic loop from corruption, requires SPICE inspection at `:5930`).

When a VM (Mac or Windows) shows a frozen/black display and SSH times out at banner exchange, **check `info status` via the qemu monitor before assuming a crash**. The Windows VM did this on 2026-05-13 (paused at 16:35, discovered 7.5h later when user noticed black screen):

```
$ (echo "info status") | socat - UNIX-CONNECT:/home/marsh-office/windows-vm/qemu-monitor.sock
VM status: paused (io-error)
```

QEMU's default `werror=stop` policy pauses the VM on the first failed disk write rather than letting the guest OS see a phantom-success and corrupt data. Symptoms match a hang exactly:
- Frozen/black display (last frame stuck)
- SSH banner-exchange timeout
- `/proc/<qemu-pid>/stat` shows utime/stime not advancing
- `/proc/<qemu-pid>/io` shows no recent writes

**Why:** Transient filesystem hiccups, qcow2 cluster-allocation issues, or actual disk problems — qemu can't tell which, so it stops to be safe. Almost always resumable if the underlying cause was transient.

**How to apply:**
1. Always check `info status` first. If `running`, the inner OS is hung — different problem.
2. If `paused (io-error)`, verify host disk space (`df -h`) and the qcow2 file (`ls -lah`, `stat`). If both fine, the pause was likely transient.
3. Resume with `(echo "cont") | socat - UNIX-CONNECT:<monitor-sock>` — then re-check `info status` 10s later; if still `running`, you're good.
4. From the guest's perspective, time effectively skipped — Windows uptime won't reset. Don't trust wall-clock-based things (TLS expirations, NTP drift) inside the VM until they self-correct.

**Watchdog idea:** Two VMs makes this >0% to recur. A 1-min cron that queries both monitor sockets and pages on `paused` is 15 lines of bash.

**Sock paths:**
- Mac: `/home/marsh-office/macos-vm/OSX-KVM/qemu-monitor.sock`
- Windows: `/home/marsh-office/windows-vm/qemu-monitor.sock`

When you write a reverse proxy with `fetch()` (undici) and read the upstream
body via `await upstream.arrayBuffer()` (or `.text()`/`.json()`), undici
**transparently decompresses** gzip/br bodies. If you then copy the upstream
`content-encoding` (e.g. `br`) and `content-length` headers onto the re-emitted
(now-plain) bytes, the browser tries to decode plain bytes as brotli/gzip →
`ERR_CONTENT_DECODING_FAILED`, and the client's `fetch` throws "Failed to fetch".

**Why:** the upstream encoding/length headers no longer describe the bytes you
re-send once undici decoded them.

**How to apply:** in the proxy header-copy loop, skip `content-encoding` and
`content-length` alongside `connection`/`transfer-encoding`/`keep-alive`.

Concrete bite (2026-05-28): Restart shop `apps/shop/src/middleware.ts` auth
proxy (`/api/auth/*` → shop-api). shop-api brotli-compresses responses; the
proxy forwarded `content-encoding: br`, so the better-auth client's sign-in
fetch threw. The session cookie WAS set (sign-in "worked"), but the success
redirect to `/account/orders` never fired — user left on the sign-in page with
no error. Fixed in `2332e4d4`. Symptom signature: login succeeds server-side
but UI doesn't advance + `ERR_CONTENT_DECODING_FAILED` in console.

**"Fetch API cannot load <url> due to access control checks" in a Tauri/WebKitGTK
webview is almost never a CORS problem.** It is WebKit's misleading label for a
`fetch()` that never got a TCP connection because **libsoup's `max-conns-per-host`
(default 6) is exhausted by long-lived SSE/EventSource streams.**

**Confirmed 2026-05-20** after ~15 wrong fix cycles. Root cause: the operator
opens 5 always-on SSE streams (Zero sync, OperatorPanel, OperatorBackgroundScanner,
intent-dispatcher, use-state-snapshots) + 1 on `/harness` + Next HMR = 7 permanent
sockets to `localhost:3055`. With ≥6 slots camped, every regular `fetch()` hangs
forever. Full plan: `apps/operator/docs/plans/webkit-sse-connection-pool-2026-05-20.md`.

**How to diagnose (do this FIRST, not last):**
- `ss -tnp | grep WebKit | grep :3055` — count ESTAB sockets. ≥6 idle = pool full.
- In-page `fetch(...)` never reaches the server (no dev-log line) while `curl` to
  the same URL returns 200 in ms → it's the pool, not the server, not CORS.

**The real fix** is reducing concurrent EventSource connections: a client-side
SSE multiplexer in `@restart/sse` (one connection, N topic subscribers), or
making non-critical streams lazy. `@restart/sse` has server fan-out (`getChannel`)
but no client multiplexer yet.

**Misdiagnoses to NOT repeat** (all tried, all failed this class of bug):
`devUrl` 127.0.0.1↔localhost, `Connection: close`, ACAO:* headers, route
prewarmers, Turbopack compile-race theories. The `devUrl: localhost` change is
harmless and fine to keep, but it does NOT fix this.

**Verification is invalid in a warm session** — the bug only reproduces on a
cold window launch. Have the user fully quit + relaunch and check first paint.
See [[feedback-search-web-before-fix-loops]].

Restart's single-node Typesense (Docker `typesense`, compose `docker-compose.typesense.yml`, project `restart`) silently took product search down from **2026-05-27 → 2026-05-28** (~36h, plus an earlier self-recovered episode 2026-04-23).

**Root cause (CONFIRMED — fd exhaustion, NOT transient I/O):** every Raft snapshot makes RocksDB hard-link all its `.sst` files; `storefront_products` has **~976 .sst files** and the process holds **~1000 fds while loaded**, against a container **nofile soft limit of 1024**. The snapshot exceeds 1024 → EMFILE → `Checkpoint creation failure, code 5` → SnapshotError → lone node steps down, can't `reset_peer` → "no leader" wedge. Recurs on EVERY snapshot. **Fix = `ulimits.nofile` soft 1024→524288** (host hard limit already 524288) in both compose files. NOT OOM (mem ~1.6G/16G), NOT disk-full (~60%), NOT mongod/CPU (I wrongly blamed mongod mid-session — it was fd all along), NOT OpenAI timeouts. `--reset-peers-on-error` + autoheal only recover the wedge after the fact; raising nofile removes the cause. Manual recovery if it ever recurs = `docker restart typesense` (reloads ~1M docs; watch `docker logs -f typesense | grep -i loaded`).

**Fix (commits on master ~2026-05-28):** `--reset-peers-on-error` (auto-recovers the wedge) + a `/health`-body healthcheck (over bash `/dev/tcp` — the `typesense/typesense:29.0` image has NO curl/wget but ships bash) + a `willfarrell/autoheal` sidecar (restart-on-unhealthy, since restart-on-exit never fires). Prod compose bumped `0.25.2 → 29.0` (0.25.2 predates the auto-embedding schema, so prod likely never built the collection and was permanently on the SQL fallback). Runbook: `docs/guides/typesense-outage-runbook.md`.

**GOTCHA (load-bearing):** the healthcheck `start_period` MUST exceed the cold reload (set to **3600s** after 900s proved too short). During reload `/health` is `{"ok":false}`; with a short start_period, autoheal marks it unhealthy and kills it mid-load → infinite restart loop that never finishes (observed live: a co-tenant `mongod` pinning ~15 cores stretched the ~12-min reload to ~20+ min and 900s let autoheal loop-kill it). A healthy node passes within seconds regardless, so a long start_period is free. NOTE: `docker restart` reuses the container's *baked-in* healthcheck config, NOT the compose file — to apply a changed `start_period` you must `docker compose up -d` (recreate), which re-triggers a reload. The running container now has 3600s + `--reset-peers-on-error` baked in.

**Write-path wedge (2026-05-28):** after the recovery, Typesense *reads/search were healthy but document WRITES hung* — a single upsert never returned and the indexer queue (`queued_writes`) wouldn't drain, while query-embedding + search worked fine. This blocks the catalog→Typesense sync pipeline, not just search. It was **transient post-recovery state**; a clean `docker compose up -d` restart cleared it and writes applied normally afterward. (Diagnosing it: test a write with `curl ...?action=upsert` + a timeout; exit 124 = wedged, 0 = healthy. Test container egress with **bash** `/dev/tcp`, never `sh`/dash — dash lacks `/dev/tcp` and gives false "no egress" negatives.)

While Typesense is down, search degrades to the Postgres FTS path — see [[project_restart_search_fts_fallback]].

endpoint, `OPENAI_API_KEY` in .env) — switched from gemini-2.5-flash for reliable native function-
calling + far fewer 503s, at ~half the (tiny) cost. SupportedModel = `qwen3.5` | `gemini-flash-2.0`
| `groq` | `gpt-4o-mini` (all selectable via the `model` param; `DEFAULT_MODEL` in scout.types.ts).
(xAI **Grok** was added then removed — git-recoverable from commit 8b82a191.)

**The fix that made gemini reliable — FORCED function-calling (Option A), in `callGemini`:** on the
FIRST detection round only, append a `respond_to_user` sentinel tool + set `tool_choice:'required'`.
gemini-2.5-flash treats native tool-calls as optional under `tool_choice:'auto'` — it would reply in
prose and SKIP the obvious tool (search/prefill/open_drawer), then sometimes hallucinate it had acted.
Forcing a choice between the real tools and the sentinel removes that escape hatch. The sentinel call
means "no action, just reply" → filtered out → the streaming prose round runs. **Force round-0 only:**
forcing every round makes the model re-call the action in a loop (open_drawer fired 5× → MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS);
later rounds use `auto` so the turn terminates. Result: search **4/4**, prefill **2/2** (3rd was a 503),
open_drawer **1×**, chitchat streams a normal reply — and the real-browser /quote prefill that used to
fail now fills the form. A deterministic detection temp (0.1) is also set.

Forced function-calling is shared by both OpenAI-compat providers (gpt-4o-mini + gemini) via the
`RESPOND_SENTINEL` const + `forceTool` on round 1. gpt-4o-mini's native function-calling is strong, so
forcing is belt-and-suspenders there; for gemini it was essential.

**Gotcha — telemetry vs the least-privilege DB role:** scout connects as **`restart_app`** (DATABASE_URL),
which has INSERT/SELECT but **NO CREATE on schema public**. `TelemetryService.ensureSchema()` ran
`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` on every boot → denied → it flipped `degraded=true` and recorded NOTHING
(cost/usage) for ALL models. Fixed: on DDL failure, probe `to_regclass` — if the tables exist (always, on
deployed DBs), keep telemetry ON (INSERTs work). Lesson: any runtime DDL under `restart_app` fails; do
schema in migrations (privileged), not at boot.

Residual flakiness on gemini is ONLY Google 503s (infra, not routing); gpt-4o-mini avoids those.

**Testing:** Scout e2e = **verdict** (Tauri docs are papercup-only — Restart has no Tauri app). Drive the
browser chat (gemini default now routes reliably), or hit `/chat/stream` with `model:"gemini-flash-2.0"`,
